look_here_first: FIRST flip a mature leaf: tiny NECTARY DOTS on UNDERSIDE = affinis; lutea has none. Both affinis and lutea lack PETIOLE glands, so don't confuse the structures. Next check small bracts under an open flower: affinis has them, lutea lacks them. Affinis's green-yellow flower is generally >25 mm wide, with wavy, clubbed outer corona tips (>10 mm). The broad cowboy-hat leaf is only a clue.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves broader than long, usually 2–3 rounded lobes

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: outer corona filaments long and sinuous

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: nectaries present on abaxial leaf surface

lookalikes.differences: P. lutea lacks floral bracts and abaxial leaf nectaries and has smaller flowers. P. foetida is much hairier, foul-smelling when rubbed, and has a conspicuous cage of finely divided involucral bracts around the flower/fruit.
